metadata.style: Sketchy-medical-style scene-based mnemonics. Per-symbol logical link via phonetic, shape, acronym, or concept. Pharmacological subfamilies share visual base; functional opposites use contrasting visuals.
design_rules: Pick the strongest link per symbol — phonetic, letter shape, acronym-as-object, conceptual association, word breakdown.
Receptor SUBFAMILIES with similar pharmacology (e.g. Gs vs Gi) get CONTRASTING visual bases.
Same concept = same recurring scene/object across all images. Different drawings of the same scene are fine.
Encode FUNCTION: agonist activates the scene; antagonist blocks/lowers/quiets it; inverse agonist reverses it.
Drugs appear as named characters/tools INSIDE the scene (the bus driver, the foreman, the postal worker).
Side effects naturally emerge from the same scene (EPS pyramids near a D2 barrier, cookies stolen near 2C, etc.).

DOPA_MINE.scene_name: DOPA-MINE Co. — coal mine extracting dopamine ore
DOPA_MINE.setting: A working coal mine. Sign at entrance: 'DOPA-MINE Co.'. Inside: 4 sections labeled by pathway — Mesolimbic (heart-shaped chamber), Mesocortical (think-bubble chamber), Nigrostriatal (motor gear chamber), Tuberoinfundibular (milk-pump chamber).
recurring_characters: Coal carts on tracks = dopamine release vesicles
Vertical machinery = D1-family receptors (elevators going UP — Gs/excitatory)
Red barriers/locks = D2-family receptors (blocking flow — Gi/inhibitory)

uses_for_pathology.psychosis: Mesolimbic chamber overflowing with carts (excess D2 stimulation)
uses_for_pathology.negative_symptoms: Mesocortical chamber empty, cobwebs (insufficient D1 stimulation)
uses_for_pathology.EPS: Nigrostriatal section: workers wearing newspaper PYRAMID hats labeled 'EXTRA' (when D2 barriers slammed too hard)
uses_for_pathology.hyperprolactinemia: Tuberoinfundibular pump SPRAYS milk when D2 barrier is closed

BUS_LINE_1A.setting: Old wooden bus-stop booth. Sign: '1A'. A frantic RABBIT (the universal anxiety creature) sits trembling on the bench.
recurring_characters: Different buses on Line 1A = different 1A partial agonists (Buspirone, Vilazodone, Vortioxetine, Aripiprazole)
Late bus = the autoreceptor delay-of-onset for SSRIs (4-6 weeks)

TAROT_2A.setting: Dim Victorian parlor. Round table with TWO Ace tarot cards (the '2A'). The reader is a tie-dye-shirted hippie. Walls swirl with psychedelic colors.
recurring_characters: Hippie reader = LSD / Psilocybin / DMT (5-HT2A agonists → hallucinations)
Officer 'Atypical PD' with a flashlight = atypical antipsychotic (turns lights off, blocks 2A)
Special officer with mirror = Pimavanserin (inverse agonist — flips the tarot cards over)

CONVENIENCE_STORE_7.setting: A 7-Eleven store, neon sign glowing at midnight. Big '7' on the door. Clock on the wall says 7:00 with both AM and PM marked.
recurring_characters: Night clerk = Lurasidone (turning off lights = blocking 5-HT7)

D1_receptor.symbol: Single elevator with '1↑' button, going UP to the PFC top floor
D1_receptor.mnemonic_link: UP arrow = excitatory (Gs/↑cAMP). Number = 1. Top floor = prefrontal cortex (working memory).

function_depiction.agonism: Elevator rides up smoothly — bright lights on each floor as it passes

D1_receptor.use_when: Discussing PFC dopamine, working memory, positive symptoms via D1

D5_receptor.symbol: Glass elevator with '5' button, ascending through 5 floors of the hippocampus department
D5_receptor.mnemonic_link: Same UP/Gs visual as D1. Number = 5. Hippocampus = memory department (5 floors of bookshelves).

function_depiction.agonism: Elevator rises through library floors, books illuminated

D2_receptor.category: Dopamine receptor — D2-family (Gi, ↓cAMP, INHIBITORY) — THE central antipsychotic target
D2_receptor.symbol: Massive RED BARRIER labeled '2' across the main mesolimbic track. A foreman stands by the lever.
D2_receptor.mnemonic_link: DOWN/blocking = inhibitory (Gi/↓cAMP). Number = 2. Mesolimbic = the psychosis track.

function_depiction.antagonism: Foreman LOWERS the barrier — carts pile up behind. EPS pyramid-hatted workers spawn nearby. Tuberoinfundibular milk-pump leaks (hyperprolactinemia).
function_depiction.partial_agonism: Barrier hovers HALFWAY (Aripiprazole, Brexpiprazole, Cariprazine — the foreman is half-asleep)
function_depiction.agonism: Barrier raised wide — runaway carts = stimulant psychosis

D2_receptor.use_when: All antipsychotics, schizophrenia, EPS, hyperprolactinemia, stimulant psychosis, tardive dyskinesia, NMS

D3_receptor.symbol: Three small red barriers in a heart-shaped (limbic) sub-chamber
D3_receptor.mnemonic_link: Same red-barrier base as D2 (Gi family). Number = 3. Heart-shaped chamber = limbic.

function_depiction.selective_partial_agonism: Cariprazine wears a name-tag and operates ONLY these three barriers — the surrounding D2 main barrier untouched (selectivity)

D3_receptor.use_when: Cariprazine, limbic dopamine selectivity, addiction circuits, anhedonia

D4_receptor.category: Dopamine receptor — D2-family (Gi, ↓cAMP) — high clozapine affinity, low EPS
D4_receptor.symbol: Four-bolt locking mechanism on a SILENT chamber door (no EPS workers around it)
D4_receptor.mnemonic_link: Same red-locked base (Gi family). Number = 4 bolts. Silence = low EPS profile.

function_depiction.antagonism: Clozapine carries a special Z-shaped key (the Z of cloZapine) that fits all 4 bolts

D4_receptor.use_when: Clozapine, novel atypicals with low EPS, theoretical ADHD pathophysiology

5-HT1A_receptor.symbol: Bus-stop sign '1A' with a trembling rabbit on the bench, awaiting a calming bus
5-HT1A_receptor.mnemonic_link: Bus-line number = 1A. Rabbit = the anxious patient. Bus arriving = anxiolysis.

function_depiction.partial_agonism: Buspirone Express bus arrives, rabbit boards, tension melts. Vilazodone, Vortioxetine, Aripiprazole = different buses on the SAME 1A line.
function_depiction.autoreceptor_role: Sometimes the bus is empty for 4-6 weeks (SSRI delay-of-onset = autoreceptor desensitization)

5-HT1A_receptor.use_when: Buspirone, vilazodone, vortioxetine, aripiprazole, SSRI delay-of-onset, partial-agonist anxiolysis

5-HT2A_receptor.category: Serotonin receptor (Gq, cortical) — psychedelic + atypical antipsychotic target
5-HT2A_receptor.symbol: Tarot table with TWO Ace cards. Tie-dye hippie reader. Psychedelic walls.
5-HT2A_receptor.mnemonic_link: 2 Ace cards = '2A'. Tarot = visions = hallucinations. Psychedelic walls = LSD/psilocybin.

function_depiction.agonism: Hippie reads the cards aloud — walls swirl wildly (LSD trip)
function_depiction.antagonism: Officer 'Atypical PD' enters with flashlight, walls fade to gray (atypical antipsychotic blockade — central to ALL atypicals)
function_depiction.inverse_agonism: Special officer with mirror flips cards face-down (Pimavanserin)

5-HT2A_receptor.use_when: All atypical antipsychotics' core mechanism, hallucinogens (LSD/psilocybin/DMT), pimavanserin, trazodone, mirtazapine

5-HT2C_receptor.symbol: Behind the tarot parlor, a kitchen with TWO chefs (the 'Cs') guarding a giant cookie jar
5-HT2C_receptor.mnemonic_link: 2 Chefs / 2 Cookies = '2C'. Active receptor = chefs vigilant, no overeating.

function_depiction.antagonism: Mirtazapine/Olanzapine/Quetiapine sneak in, KO the chefs, eat all cookies → patient gains weight
function_depiction.agonism: Lorcaserin (now withdrawn) makes chefs hyper-vigilant → weight loss

5-HT2C_receptor.use_when: Weight gain side effects of mirtazapine/olanzapine/quetiapine; trazodone; lorcaserin (historical)

5-HT3_receptor.category: Serotonin receptor — UNIQUE: ligand-gated ion channel, not G-protein. CTZ + gut.
5-HT3_receptor.symbol: Three mighty IRON GATES (literally drawn as channels, not G-proteins) bursting open with green vomit-water
5-HT3_receptor.mnemonic_link: 3 = three gates. Iron channel = ionotropic (the only 5-HT receptor that is). Green water = nausea/vomiting from CTZ.

function_depiction.antagonism: Three identical PLUGS (Ondansetron the prototype) seal the gates. Mirtazapine and Vortioxetine carry plugs too (their antiemetic side effect).
function_depiction.agonism: Excess serotonin (e.g. SSRI side effect) = gates flood open → diarrhea/nausea

5-HT3_receptor.use_when: Nausea/vomiting, mirtazapine antiemetic effect, vortioxetine, chemotherapy nausea, SSRI GI side effects

5-HT6_receptor.symbol: Library back-room with SIX framed PhD diplomas on the wall. An old professor sits reading.
5-HT6_receptor.mnemonic_link: 6 = SIX (sixth sense, six diplomas). Professor = cognition.

function_depiction.antagonism: Vortioxetine the professor sharpens his glasses — pro-cognitive effect

5-HT6_receptor.use_when: Cognition in schizophrenia/depression, vortioxetine's cognitive edge, theoretical procognitive targets

5-HT7_receptor.symbol: A 7-Eleven store glowing at midnight, sign reads 'OPEN 24/7'
5-HT7_receptor.mnemonic_link: 7 = the store's name and hours. 24/7 = circadian (always running).

function_depiction.antagonism: Lurasidone the night-clerk turns off neon signs and locks doors — restored sleep-wake balance, antidepressant effect

5-HT7_receptor.use_when: Lurasidone, vortioxetine (also hits 7), circadian rhythm disorders, bipolar depression sleep architecture

SERT.symbol: A POSTAL CARRIER in a uniform reading 'SERT' (Service & Reuptake Transporter), collecting serotonin packages from synapse mailboxes
SERT.mnemonic_link: SERT = Service. Postal worker = pickup-and-return = re-uptake.

function_depiction.blockade: SSRI tapes a 'NO PICKUPS TODAY' sign on every mailbox. Packages pile up in synapse (more serotonin available). Postal carrier paces frustrated for 4-6 weeks until he gives up (delay of onset).

SERT.use_when: All SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs (some), vortioxetine, SARIs, antidepressant onset delay
